{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-ks-c","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"60eee99f31acd242e7de32f2a4858fd32035836f3f8c78ce8dd12c41a01acc43","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-ks-class-c:lineage:55","source_registry_sha256":"c7fb2073a9e8bb6a73d0151458fe04991b703d84f882b00a01bedfcea433c383","source_liveness_sha256":"94328be42cc10cf86af8e486b41bc40c72c45e4700d27b9b46d1f3d2feac7bb6"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C2"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C2","chunk_id":"C2.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Weather and trip planning","heading":"C2 — Weather and trip planning","learner_facing":false,"markdown":"## C2 — Weather and trip planning

FACT_ID: sec12-R01 | anchor: A109
Prepare the vehicle before winter weather, including suitable tires before the first snowfall. [A109]
Source: [A109 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0109]

FACT_ID: sec12-R02 | anchor: A109
For front-wheel-drive vehicles, the handbook recommends winter or all-season tires on all four wheels rather than only the front. [A109]
Source: [A109 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0109]

FACT_ID: sec12-R03 | anchor: A109
The handbook permits studded tires only from November 1 through April 1. [A109]
Source: [A109 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0109]

FACT_ID: sec12-R04 | anchor: A109
During an ice or snowstorm, especially with a weather advisory, drive only when absolutely necessary. [A109]
Source: [A109 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0109]

FACT_ID: sec12-R05 | anchor: A109
Before necessary winter travel, clear snow and ice from lights, windows and wipers. [A109]
Source: [A109 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0109]

FACT_ID: sec12-R06 | anchor: A109
Use freeze-resistant windshield-cleaning fluid and keep its reservoir adequately filled. [A109]
Source: [A109 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0109]

FACT_ID: sec12-R07 | anchor: A109
Drive slowly in winter conditions and do not outpace cautious traffic merely because the vehicle seems to have good grip. [A109]
Source: [A109 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0109]

FACT_ID: sec12-R08 | anchor: A109
Expect bridges, ramps and overpasses to freeze early as sleet, freezing rain or snow begins. [A109]
Source: [A109 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0109]

FACT_ID: sec12-R09 | anchor: A109
Slippery patches may persist after road crews clear other pavement. [A109]
Source: [A109 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0109]

FACT_ID: sec12-R10 | anchor: A109
Keep an emergency survival kit in the vehicle and replenish supplies after using them. [A109]
Source: [A109 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0109]

FACT_ID: sec12-R11 | anchor: A109
The winter kit should include an inflated spare, shovel, jumper cables, towing and tire chains, traction sand or salt and tools. [A109]
Source: [A109 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0109]

FACT_ID: sec12-R12 | anchor: A109
Pack a working flashlight and batteries, reflective triangles, bright cloth, a compass and first-aid supplies. [A109]
Source: [A109 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0109]

FACT_ID: sec12-R13 | anchor: A109
Include windshield-cleaning supplies, an ice scraper, snow brush, waterproof-stored matches, blankets and warm clothing. [A109]
Source: [A109 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0109]

FACT_ID: sec12-R14 | anchor: A109
Carry water and shelf-stable energy foods such as dried fruit, unsalted nuts or hard candy. [A109]
Source: [A109 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0109]

FACT_ID: sec12-R15 | anchor: A109
If stranded in cold weather, remain with the vehicle unless the location and distance to help are both known exactly. [A109]
Source: [A109 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0109]

FACT_ID: sec12-R16 | anchor: A109
When cold-weather stranding occurs, remain calm, wait for assistance and turn on hazard lights. [A109]
Source: [A109 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0109]

FACT_ID: sec12-R17 | anchor: A109
For visibility while stranded, the handbook recommends two flares at safe distances, one at either end, and bright cloth on the driver-side window, mirror or handle. [A109]
Source: [A109 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0109]

FACT_ID: sec12-R18 | anchor: A109
Keep the exhaust outlet clear of snow and debris because trapped exhaust can cause unconsciousness or death. [A109]
Source: [A109 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0109]

FACT_ID: sec12-R19 | anchor: A109
For cold stranding, the handbook suggests warming the vehicle intermittently, about 10 minutes per hour while fuel remains, with a clear exhaust and a partly open window for ventilation. [A109]
Source: [A109 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0109]

FACT_ID: sec12-R20 | anchor: A109
Even in extreme cold, leave at least one window partly open during the described stranding response because inadequate ventilation can allow carbon monoxide poisoning. [A109]
Source: [A109 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0109]

FACT_ID: sec12-R21 | anchor: A109
At least one stranded occupant should remain awake. [A109]
Source: [A109 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0109]

FACT_ID: sec12-R22 | anchor: A109
Use blankets and wool clothing to protect against frostbite and hypothermia while stranded. [A109]
Source: [A109 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0109]

FACT_ID: sec12-R23 | anchor: A110
In very hot conditions, check tire mounting and pressure and inspect tires every two hours or 100 miles. [A110]
Source: [A110 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0110]

FACT_ID: sec12-R24 | anchor: A110
Tire pressure rises with heat; do not release air just because the hot-tire pressure has risen, since cooling would leave pressure too low. [A110]
Source: [A110 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0110]

FACT_ID: sec12-R25 | anchor: A110
Maintain sufficient engine oil and, if equipped, monitor the oil-temperature gauge for its proper range. [A110]
Source: [A110 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0110]

FACT_ID: sec12-R26 | anchor: A110
Before hot-weather driving, ensure adequate coolant, and monitor the coolant-temperature gauge while traveling. [A110]
Source: [A110 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0110]

FACT_ID: sec12-R27 | anchor: A110
If coolant temperature exceeds its highest safe range, stop as soon as safely possible and investigate rather than continuing toward possible engine failure or fire. [A110]
Source: [A110 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0110]

FACT_ID: sec12-R28 | anchor: A110
Surface tar can soften and rise in very hot weather, creating slick spots that require caution. [A110]
Source: [A110 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0110]

FACT_ID: sec12-R29 | anchor: A110
High speed adds tire and engine heat, so choose a slower speed where needed to avoid overheating in very hot conditions. [A110]
Source: [A110 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0110]

FACT_ID: sec12-R30 | anchor: A110
Do not seek tornado shelter under a bridge or overpass because it offers little protection from flying objects. [A110]
Source: [A110 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0110]

FACT_ID: sec12-R31 | anchor: A110
The handbook identifies a well-built building with plumbing and electrical wiring as the safest thunderstorm shelter. [A110]
Source: [A110 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0110]

FACT_ID: sec12-R32 | anchor: A110
In its hard-top-vehicle lightning instructions, the handbook directs closing doors, raising windows, avoiding metal surfaces and not using a radio connected to an external vehicle antenna. [A110]
Source: [A110 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0110]

Misconceptions: Daily trip-duration guidance is not a statutory driving-hours limit; good winter tires do not remove other traffic and visibility risks; a hot tire's increased pressure is not a reason to bleed it; severe-weather shelter advice has explicit unresolved conditions.
Mnemonics: Editorial cue: plan, inspect, equip, reassess. It organizes preparation without adding weather thresholds or escape instructions.
Glossary: Distinguish trip-planning estimate, survival kit, freeze-resistant washer fluid, coolant warning, bleeding tar and severe-weather source debt using the fact blocks.
Dynamic facts: Conditions change during a trip. Equipment recommendations depend on the vehicle manual; edition-bound tire dates and emergency procedures require issuer refresh. No current weather forecast or unverified rescue technique is asserted.
